VPS Server Locations Explained (2026): How to Choose New Jersey, Los Angeles or Dallas

By ZedgeHost Team · 25 November 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: pick the VPS location closest to most of your users. New Jersey suits a US East Coast audience and Europe-facing traffic, Los Angeles suits a US West Coast audience and Asia-Pacific-facing traffic, and Dallas suits an audience spread across the whole US. If your visitors are in Pakistan, all three US locations are a similar distance away, so the plan size matters more than the city. At ZedgeHost the choice of location is free, and VPS plans start at Rs 1,699 per month.

Why your VPS location matters

Every request to your website travels from your visitor to your server and back again. The longer that distance, the longer the round trip takes. This delay is called latency, and it affects how fast a page starts loading for the visitor. A server close to your users answers faster than the same server on the other side of the world.

The reason is physics. Data travels through fibre at a large fraction of the speed of light, and every extra stretch of cable adds time. As a rough rule of thumb, each 100 miles of fibre adds about 1 millisecond, before routing and processing are counted. That is why the city you pick is a real decision, not a cosmetic one, and it is also why no location can beat the distance between your server and your audience.

Location is one of several things to get right when you move up from shared hosting. If you are still deciding between the two, read shared hosting vs VPS hosting in Pakistan first, then come back and pick your location.

The three ZedgeHost VPS locations at a glance

ZedgeHost VPS servers are available in three US locations. All three run the same four plans at the same prices, and the choice of location costs nothing extra. What differs is which audience each one serves best.

New Jersey: the East Coast choice

New Jersey sits in the New York metro area, one of the densest internet regions in the world. It is the natural pick when most of your visitors are on the US East Coast: New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Washington, and the south-eastern states. It is also the best of the three for traffic coming from Europe, because the trans-Atlantic cables land on this coast. If your customers are American businesses on the East Coast, or European visitors reaching a US server, New Jersey is the straightforward choice.

Los Angeles: the West Coast and Pacific choice

Los Angeles faces the Pacific, and the submarine cables from Asia and Australia come ashore in California and the Pacific Northwest. That makes it the pick for a West Coast audience in California, Oregon, and Washington, and for visitors from Japan, Korea, Singapore, and Australia. If your app serves users on both the US West Coast and Asia-Pacific, Los Angeles gives both groups the shortest path of the three locations.

Dallas: the central choice for a nationwide audience

Dallas sits near the geographic centre of the US. Its longest path to any American city is far shorter than a coast-to-coast path, so no part of the country is badly served. If your visitors are spread from New York to California and you can only pick one location, Dallas is the safe middle ground. It is also a practical pick for apps whose users are in the central states, or for services with short paths into Mexico.

How to choose your VPS location in 4 steps

Picking a location takes a few minutes if you work through it in order:

  1. Find where your visitors are. Check your analytics for the countries and regions your visitors come from. If you have no traffic yet, use where your customers live: a store selling in the US East Coast, a SaaS product with users in California, or a community spread across the US.
  2. Match the closest region. East Coast audience means New Jersey, West Coast means Los Angeles, and a nationwide audience means Dallas. When two regions are close in size, pick the one with your paying customers, not your casual readers.
  3. Check what your server talks to. If your app calls a database, a payment gateway, or another API on every request, the server should sit close to that service too. A fast link to your users does not help if every page waits on a database across the country.
  4. Test after you deploy. Once the server is running, load your site from the places your audience lives and check how fast pages start loading. If the numbers look wrong for your main audience, that is the time to reconsider, before the server fills up with live data.

When location matters less

Location is not the whole story. If your site is mostly static pages served through a CDN, the CDN answers most requests from a cache near the visitor, and the origin server location matters far less. The same goes for background jobs, scheduled tasks, and backups, which do not wait on a visitor. In those cases, pick the plan with the right CPU, RAM, and storage, and treat location as a secondary choice.

Visitors in Pakistan are a special case. All three ZedgeHost VPS locations are in the US, so they are a similar distance from Pakistan, and the difference between them is small for a Pakistani audience. If your visitors are mostly in Pakistan, choose on plan size and price, add a CDN if you serve a global audience, and consider cloud hosting or shared hosting if your site does not need a full server. Operating system options

At order time you choose the operating system for your VPS: AlmaLinux, Ubuntu, or Debian. If you prefer to install your own system, choose the empty disk option instead. The choice is free on all four plans, so pick the system your app and your team already know, and keep the server setup simple.

Can you change location later?

A VPS is tied to the datacenter where it is created, so changing location means setting up a new server in the new location and moving your sites and data to it. That is why it is worth choosing carefully at order time. If you are moving a website from another host, free website migration is included in every ZedgeHost plan, and the step-by-step move is covered in how to move your website to a new host without downtime.

The short version: match the location to your audience, match the plan to your workload, and test after deploy. New Jersey for the East Coast and Europe, Los Angeles for the West Coast and Asia-Pacific, Dallas for a nationwide audience, and the plan size decides the rest.
